diagnosis.root_cause: A security-group change pushed by the cloud infrastructure team blocked outbound TCP connections from the payments-gateway service to the external payment processor processor.acme-pay.com, leading to outbound connection timeouts and 100% payment authorization failures.
evidence: outbound connection to processor.acme-pay.com timing out (connect timeout 10s)
100% of payment authorizations failing: upstream connect timeout
DNS resolves processor.acme-pay.com fine; TCP connect never completes
diagnosis.recommended_fix: Review and revert the security-group change made this morning by the cloud infrastructure team to restore outbound TCP connectivity from the payments-gateway to processor.acme-pay.com.

evidence.plan_reasoning: The incident report indicates card payments are failing at checkout and mentions a cloud infrastructure security-group change made this morning. I will check the payment_auth_success_rate metric on the payments-gateway service to quantify the failure pattern.

The payment_auth_success_rate for payments-gateway dropped sharply starting at 11:08 UTC, confirming the incident timeline. I will now query the outbound_connect_errors_per_s metric on the same service to determine if the failures are due to connection timeouts or downstream refusal.

Outbound connect errors surge starting at 11:08 UTC, coinciding with the drop in payment success rate. Given the incident report mentions a security-group change by the cloud-infra team this morning, I will search the logs for payments-gateway to look for connection timeout or network refusal errors.

evidence.result:
5 runbook section(s):

[1] connection-pool-exhaustion.md > Symptoms (score 0.358)
Errors or log lines stating that a connection pool is exhausted, that all
connections are in use, or that acquisition timed out with many waiters queued.
Pool wait time rises sharply. Throughput collapses while CPU and memory may look
normal, because requests are blocked waiting for a connection rather than doing
work.

[2] certificate-and-config-expiry.md > Symptoms (score 0.343)
A sudden, total failure that starts at a round wall-clock time with no deploy and
no traffic change. Errors mention an expired certificate, an invalid or expired
token, a signature failure, or an authentication rejection. Often affects every
request on a path at once, and may hit several services that share the same
certificate or credential.

[3] connection-pool-exhaustion.md > Mitigation (score 0.3212)
Relieve the downstream slowdown or cut the offending traffic. Then isolate pools
per dependency, size them for peak concurrency, add acquisition timeouts, and fix
any code path that fails to release a connection.

[4] connection-pool-exhaustion.md > Likely causes (score 0.3105)
- A slow downstream (database, cache, or another service) holding connections
  longer, so the fixed-size pool drains and cannot refill fast enough.
- Retry amplification increasing concurrent outbound calls beyond the pool size.
- A connection leak: connections checked out and never returned due to a missing
  release in an error path.
- Pool sized too small for current traffic, or a single pool shared between fast
  local work and slow remote calls.

[5] connection-pool-exhaustion.md > How to confirm (score 0.3046)
- Check pool metrics: active connections at the ceiling, waiters greater than
  zero, rising acquisition wait time.
- Correlate with downstream latency and with the caller's outbound request rate.
- If downstream latency is normal, suspect a leak; look for steadily falling idle
  connections over time.
